text.paragraph: New patient with a right upper abdominal mass, aching and weight loss: work-up of a liver mass, symptom care, and how he wants to receive results. Concerns: He has had a dull ache under his right ribs, early fullness and weight loss for three months, and can feel a firm lump there himself; As a physician by training he wants to see his images and results himself, to be told plainly, and to be cared for on the same pathway as any other patient; He wants to keep working and traveling for as long as he can. [S]

list.item: Right upper quadrant abdominal mass with weight loss: a dull ache under the right ribs and early fullness for about three months, 4 kg weight loss, and a firm, non-tender mass felt 4 cm below the right costal margin; no jaundice, fever, or itching. Ultrasound today: a 6.8 cm solid, heterogeneous mass in liver segments IV and V that cannot be separated from the gallbladder, which contains stones; the rest of the liver is smooth, with no ascites. Multiphase CT, tumor markers, hepatitis serology and medical oncology consultation arranged: resolved, confirmed [S]

Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder invading the liver: core biopsy of the liver mass shows moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (CK7 positive, CK20 and CDX2 negative), and multiphase CT and MRI show a 7.1 cm mass arising from the gallbladder fundus and invading liver segments IVb and V, with gallstones and two enlarged nodes in the hepatoduodenal ligament; no cirrhosis; alpha-fetoprotein normal, CA 19-9 raised. Clinical T3 N1 before staging laparoscopy (AJCC 8th edition). Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented final illness, described in life as liver cancer and at autopsy as gallbladder adenocarcinoma: active, confirmed [S]

Resolved hepatitis B infection: hepatitis B surface antigen negative, total core antibody positive, surface antibody positive, HBV DNA undetectable; hepatitis C antibody negative. At risk of reactivation during chemotherapy and immunotherapy; monitored: active, confirmed [S]

Peritoneal metastases from gallbladder adenocarcinoma: several 3 to 6 mm nodules on the parietal peritoneum and omentum at staging laparoscopy, biopsy positive for adenocarcinoma of the same type; stage IVB (M1), not resectable: active, confirmed [S]

Acute viral upper respiratory infection on day 10 of cycle 5 of chemoimmunotherapy: sore throat, runny nose and dry cough for three days, afebrile, with a neutrophil count of 1.6 x10^3/uL; rapid tests for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza negative; no sign of pneumonia or pneumonitis; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

Biopsy and imaging results and medical oncology consultation; diagnosis, staging plan, and hepatitis B status
Staging laparoscopy result and tumor board recommendation; first cycle of chemoimmunotherapy and specialist palliative care
Before cycle 4: restaging CT, tumor marker, toxicity review, hepatitis B monitoring, and genomic profiling result
Before cycle 8: restaging CT, toxicity review, low magnesium, and the plan for maintenance durvalumab

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Work-up of the liver mass: multiphase contrast CT of the liver with CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; MRI of the liver with MRCP if CT does not settle the origin; alpha-fetoprotein, CA 19-9 and CEA; hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody, and hepatitis C antibody; liver function with Child-Pugh and ALBI scoring; and image-guided core biopsy, because a mass in a liver without cirrhosis cannot be diagnosed by imaging alone
Medical oncology consultation for a solid liver mass with weight loss: diagnosis, staging, multidisciplinary tumor board review, and treatment

Symptom care during the work-up: acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day, small frequent meals with a dietitian's advice, weight at every visit, and a same-day call for jaundice, fever, vomiting, dark urine or worse pain; results shared with him in full as they arrive, by one coordinating clinician

Staging laparoscopy before any attempt at resection, with biopsy of any peritoneal disease and an implanted port under the same anesthetic; if no metastases, extended cholecystectomy with resection of liver segments IVb and V and portal lymphadenectomy; comprehensive genomic profiling of the biopsy tissue (HER2, mismatch repair and microsatellite status, BRAF, FGFR2, IDH1, NTRK, RET, KRAS, tumor mutational burden)

Hepatitis B reactivation monitoring for resolved infection (surface antigen negative, core antibody positive, HBV DNA undetectable): HBV DNA and ALT every 3 months during treatment and for at least 6 to 12 months after, with entecavir started promptly if HBV DNA becomes detectable or surface antigen reappears

First-line systemic therapy for stage IVB gallbladder adenocarcinoma: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 with durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1 every 21 days for up to 8 cycles, then durvalumab 1,500 mg every 4 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity; blood count, creatinine, magnesium and liver tests before each dose; TSH every cycle; CA 19-9 each cycle; CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every 2 to 3 months; teaching on immune-related side effects; ondansetron at home

Specialist palliative care alongside cancer treatment from the diagnosis of advanced disease: symptoms, nutrition, coping, goals of care, a health care agent, and a family meeting if and when he chooses
Magnesium oxide 400 mg by mouth daily for cisplatin-related low magnesium, rechecked with each dose; durvalumab maintenance every 4 weeks after the eighth cycle, with restaging CT every 2 to 3 months
Tissue diagnosis and complete staging within four weeks of the first visit
Biopsy diagnosis in nine days and staging complete by laparoscopy in about three and a half weeks
Right upper abdominal pain at 3 of 10 or less, with full days of work possible (ECOG 0 to 1)
Ache 0 to 2 of 10 on acetaminophen as needed; ECOG 1 throughout
Weight held within 2 kg of the weight at the start of treatment
60.0 kg at cycle 1 and 59.6 kg at cycle 8
Goals of care and a health care agent documented, and revisited as treatment changes
Agent named and goals recorded with palliative care and at the preventive visit
Complete first-line chemoimmunotherapy without grade 3 or higher toxicity
Seven cycles given by the last visit with grade 1 toxicity only; the eighth started that day
